2.11.5.en: * If Phinehas, by his zeal in killing the evildoer, appeased the wrath of God, does not Jesus, who did not slay another but "gave himself a ransom for all" (1 Tim 2:6), take away the wrath of God against humanity?

2.11.6.en: St. Cyril of Jerusalem * If we are conformed to His death, sin certainly becomes a lifeless corpse in us, by the spear of Baptism, just like the adulterer who was cast down through the zeal of Phinehas.

2.12.0.en: St. Gregory of Nyssa And this have ye done again, covering the altar of the LORD with tears, with weeping, and with crying out, insomuch that he regardeth not the offering any more, or receiveth it with good will at your hand. [13]

2.12.1.en: In order to marry pagan women, the believers divorced their wives to make room for achieving their own desires. Even the men who did not divorce their believing wives treated them bitterly because of their attachment to the pagan women. The wives had nothing left but to complain with tears and the cry of a bitter heart, so the altar was covered with these bitter tears. Worship in the Temple, especially on feast days, turned into grief and tears instead of rejoicing in the Lord.

2.12.2.en: The offerings and sacrifices were no longer the delight of the Lord, because they ascended floating in the tears of the wives who were overpowered and wronged, and their cries rose out of them, just as the blood of Abel cried out silently against Cain!

2.12.3.en: Perhaps marriage to pagan women corrupted the concepts of worship, so that instead of the sacrifice being linked with praise and spiritual joy, it was linked with shouting and with a man cutting his body with swords and lances until the blood gushed out on the altar (1 Kgs 18:28). As the prophet Ezekiel says: "There sat women weeping for Tammuz" (Ezek 8:14).

2.12.4.en: Instead of worshiping with their believing wives in joy and praises, so that their prayers and their offerings lifted up with pure hands would not be hindered, the men resorted to pagan wives and worshiped with them in a spirit of gloom.

2.12.5.en: Perhaps the tears and wailing here are because these treacherous men felt their error, so they offer tears without abandoning their attachment to the pagan women. They practice the worship of God to satisfy their consciences, and they practice pagan worship because of their attachment to the pagan women. They mix light with darkness. As Elijah the prophet said: "How long halt ye between two opinions? if the LORD be God, follow him: but if Baal, then follow him" (1 Kgs 18:21). And the Apostle Paul says: "For what fellowship hath righteousness with unrighteousness? and what communion hath light with darkness? And what concord hath Christ with Belial? or what part hath he that believeth with an infidel?" (2 Cor 6:14-15)

2.12.6.en: * "What communion hath light with darkness?" Where there is distinction and an irreconcilable opposition between light and darkness, whoever shares in both has a portion in neither, because of the opposition between the two parts, each against the other, at the same time in his life, which is a mixture of the two. By his faith he draws on the part that gives light, but by his dark habits he extinguishes the lamp of the mind. Since it is impossible for light and darkness to be in fellowship together, the person who embraces both is an enemy to himself, being divided against himself, divided between the two ways of virtue and evil. He sets up within himself a battle between opposites. And since, when there are two enemies, both cannot be victorious, and the victory of one leads to the death of the opponent, this civil war causes disturbance in his life. And the stronger side cannot prevail unless the other is completely destroyed.

2.13.s.en: 6. Breaking the covenant with the wife:

2.13.0.en: 14 Yet ye say, "Wherefore?" Because the LORD hath been witness between thee and the wife of thy youth, against whom thou hast dealt treacherously: yet is she thy companion, and the wife of thy covenant. 15 And did not he make one? Yet had he the residue of the spirit. And wherefore one? That he might seek a godly seed. Therefore take heed to your spirit, and let none deal treacherously against the wife of his youth. 16 "For the LORD, the God of Israel, saith that he hateth putting away: for one covereth violence with his garment, saith the LORD of hosts: therefore take heed to your spirit, that ye deal not treacherously."

2.13.2.en: Because the LORD hath been witness between thee and the wife of thy youth, against whom thou hast dealt treacherously: yet is she thy companion, and the wife of thy covenant. [14]

2.13.3.en: Again, the men behaved with a spirit of treachery and betrayal, for they married pagan women or took them as concubines, so that these would share with the wives their rights in their husbands' hearts, and also enjoy a fitting standard of living. This shameful conduct will not bring peace and joy, but inward gloom and distress.

2.13.4.en: God cares for the family; in the marriage contract He counts Himself a witness to it, so whoever dissolves this bond is like one who has broken a pledge to which God Himself bears witness. Every betrayal of this pledge has the Lord Himself as its witness. And whoever keeps the pledge with sincerity of heart and fitting conduct is counted faithful in the things of God.

2.13.5.en: He calls her "the wife of thy youth," since he loved her in his youth, so why does he ignore this love and esteem for her in his old age?

2.13.6.en: He also calls her "thy companion," that is, one who shares with him in her husband's joys and sorrows; they share together in managing all the affairs of the family, she feels responsibility with him, and she supports him as a helper to him.

2.13.7.en: "The wife of thy covenant," that is, the husband was bound to her with a firm bond, and she entered with him into a binding covenant in the most minute matters, so it is fitting for both to fulfill what they pledged.

2.13.8.en: And did not he make one? Yet had he the residue of the spirit.

2.13.9.en: And wherefore one? That he might seek a godly seed.

2.14.0.en: Therefore take heed to your spirit, and let none deal treacherously against the wife of his youth. [15]

2.14.1.en: He gives us the reasons that oblige the spouses to live together to the end in holy love, esteem, and peace. God created one Eve for one Adam, so that man would not think of another wife. As it is written in the book of Leviticus: "Neither shalt thou take a wife to her sister, to vex her, to uncover her nakedness, beside the other in her lifetime" (Lev 18:18).

2.14.2.en: God could have created another Eve, but He wanted Adam to be occupied with "seeking a godly seed," that is, to have holy children who bear the image of God. What occupies him is not the lusts of the body, to satisfy them with this woman and that, but the establishing of a holy home in which there is mutual respect in the Lord and faithfulness in love, without one betraying the other by giving his feelings to someone else. This is the natural Law and the divine Law, that "every man have his own wife" (1 Cor 7:2), living together in chastity and purity, in a holy family, bringing forth offspring that worships God" (Ps 22:30). Thus "the bed [is] undefiled" (Heb 13:4).

2.14.3.en: * In the Gospel of Matthew He says: "Whosoever shall put away his wife, saving for the cause of fornication, causeth her to commit adultery" (Mt 5:32). He who marries a woman divorced from her husband is also counted as one who has committed adultery. In any case, the Creator does not allow those whom He joined to be separated except for the cause of fornication. Moses himself, in another passage, lays down a law that a man who marries a girl after violating her by force has no right to put away his wife (Deut 22:28-29). Now if the compulsory marriage that takes place after the use of violence remains forever, how much more the voluntary marriage, which is the fruit of agreement! This is the law of the prophet: "Do not leave the wife of thy youth." Thus you see Christ naturally following the way of the Creator in every place, whether in permitting divorce or forbidding it. You see Him also protecting marriage, whatever way you flee to. He forbids divorce, since He wants marriage not to be violated, and He permits divorce when marriage is stained by unfaithfulness. It befits you to be ashamed when you refuse to unite those whom your Christ unites.

2.14.4.en: * I draw your attention to the law of one wife. The very origin of the human race in the book of Genesis establishes this (Gen 1:27). It is very clear that God ordained this (one wife) from the beginning as a pattern for the generations that followed. For after He created Adam and saw the necessity of providing a helper for him, He took one rib from his ribs (Gen 2:21-22). He appointed for the man one woman only.

2.14.5.en: * Where shall we find language able to express fittingly the happiness of that marriage which the Church binds, which the offering confirms, which the blessing ordains and seals, which the angels celebrate, and which the Father approves? For young people on all the earth have no right to marry without the consent of their parents. What kind of yoke is this of two believers who share together one hope, one desire, one discipline, and one service? They enjoy kinship in the Spirit and in the flesh. They are fellow servants together, without conflict in their concerns. Rightly they are two in one flesh (Gen 2:24; Mt 19:5; Eph 5:31). Where the flesh is one, the spirit is also one. They pray together, fast together, teach together in fellowship, beseech together, and lift up their hands together. In the Church of God they occupy an equal place (Rom 12:15; 15:6; Gal 3:28; 1 Cor 12:12). They stand equally at the table of God, in troubles, in the face of persecutions, and in their refreshment. Neither hides anything from the other, neither ignores the other, and neither causes trouble to the other.

2.14.6.en: Tertullian the Scholar * Do not count it lawful to leave, after marriage, her who is without blemish. For He says: "Take heed to your spirit, and let none deal treacherously against the wife of his youth, for she is the partner of your life, and the remnant of your spirit. I, and no other, have made her" (cf. Mal 2:14-15). The Lord says: "What therefore God hath joined together, let not man put asunder" (Mt 19:6).

2.14.7.en: The Didascalia For the LORD, the God of Israel, saith that he hateth putting away: for one covereth violence with his garment, saith the LORD of hosts.

2.15.0.en: Therefore take heed to your spirit, that ye deal not treacherously. [16]

2.15.1.en: What is truly grave is the attempt to hide their evil conduct and the treachery and betrayal in their hearts by pretending before others that they love their wives and show kindness to them, and cover them with their garments. They hide their evils and their injustice as with a garment.

2.15.2.en: God permitted the Jews to divorce because of the hardness of their hearts (Mt 19:8), but He hates it, especially since they were allowing "a man to put away his wife for every cause" (Mt 19:3).

2.15.3.en: The prophet affirms that in divorcing a wife for any cause, and in marrying a second while the first is alive, there is treachery, not only against the first wife, but it is a crime of treachery directed against God, who established the Law of holy marriage.

2.15.4.en: The Lord Christ came to raise the believers to the level of spiritual maturity and serious responsibility, so that a man would not divorce his wife except for the cause of fornication.

2.15.5.en: St. Augustine comments on the words of the Lord concerning not divorcing, saying:

2.15.6.en: [The Mosaic law did not command divorce, but commanded the one who divorces his wife to give her a certificate of divorce, because in giving her a certificate of divorce there is something that calms the rage of a man's anger.

2.15.7.en: For the Lord, who commanded those of hardened heart to give a certificate of divorce, indicated that He did not wish for divorce as far as possible. Therefore when the Lord Himself was asked about this matter, He answered, saying: "Moses because of the hardness of your hearts suffered you" (Mt 19:8), for however great the hardness of heart of him who wishes to divorce his wife, when he knows that by means of the certificate of divorce she can marry another, his anger subsides and he does not divorce her.

2.15.8.en: And to confirm this principle, that a wife is not to be divorced lightly, the Lord of glory made the only exception the cause of fornication. He commanded that all the other troubles be endured with steadfastness for the sake of conjugal love and for the sake of chastity, and the Lord of glory confirmed the same principle by calling the one who marries a divorced woman an "adulterer."]

2.16.0.en: Ye have wearied the LORD with your words.

2.16.1.en: Yet ye say, Wherein have we wearied him?

2.16.2.en: When ye say, Every one that doeth evil is good in the sight of the LORD, and he delighteth in them;

2.16.3.en: or, Where is the God of judgment? [17]

2.16.4.en: He says: "Ye have wearied the LORD with your words." They offered excuses and justifications for their sinful conduct, as though they did not recognize their grievous faults. The holy God, who desires His people to be holy, as holy children, grieves over them because of their lack of discernment, for they count evil as good work, and think that whatever they do, they are the delight of God. And if He is angry at their conduct, which in their eyes is good, they ascribe to God injustice and lack of fairness.

2.16.5.en: How astonishing! Man stands in the position of the judge, not only to judge his brother, but even to judge God Himself, saying: "Where is the God of judgment?"

2.16.6.en: Make the believer a holy leader!

2.16.7.en: * You created everything for the sake of man, and You made him a head and a king, with authority.

2.16.8.en: You desire every person to be a holy leader!

2.16.9.en: * For man's sake You established much, and by his fall You cursed the earth, and it brought forth thorns and thistles!

2.16.10.en: You desire every believer to be a secret of blessing to many.

2.16.11.en: Because of Joseph You blessed the house of Potiphar, his master.

2.16.12.en: And for the sake of David Your servant You blessed Solomon.

2.16.13.en: And because of Jonah the fugitive nature was stirred up, and the sailors lost their provisions and their peace, and almost lost their very lives.

2.16.14.en: Sanctify me and draw me to You, O Holy One.

2.16.15.en: Draw many to You by Your Holy Spirit.

2.16.16.en: * Grant me not to betray Your covenant, but let it be to me a secret of life and peace.

2.16.17.en: By Your new covenant You grant me resurrection from death, and bestow on me peace at the level of heaven!

2.16.18.en: * Let Your commandment be the constitution of my life, and Your word ever on my lips, that I may enjoy the knowledge of You, and bear witness to it by the power of the Spirit.

2.16.19.en: * Grant me not to betray my brethren, but to be faithful to You in my relationship with my brethren and my family.

2.16.20.en: Dwell in the midst of Your Church which is in my heart, and be manifested in the church of my home!

2.16.21.en: * Take away from me all treachery against the covenant, cleanse me of every abomination, and let Your Kingdom be established within me, that I may be wholly Yours, and live as befits a son of Yours.

2.16.22.en: And I commit myself to respond to Your Holy Spirit.
